editorial:
Imagine moving to LA to make it big as an artist, only to find yourself broke and lonely. That is exactly where you start with the two main characters in this flick. They are both struggling to get noticed until they encounter Cupid, a weird computer virus that seems to know everything about them. At first, it feels like a helpful digital matchmaker, but things quickly turn creepy. The vibe is a mix of modern tech anxiety and old-school scary movies, making you wonder if you should just throw your laptop in the trash. 

The acting is great because the characters feel like real people you would actually know. The pacing stays quick, though a few scenes in the middle drag a bit. You will love the twists that keep you guessing until the very end. If you are into tech-horror, you should definitely check this out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the digital glitch effects clearly. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for a movie this stylish.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out Cupid is not just a virus, but a digital monster that feeds on human obsession. It traps the two artists inside a virtual world to keep them forever. The twist is that one artist escapes by deleting their own digital identity, which kills the virus. However, the movie ends with a scare as a new download starts on a random phone, showing the virus is still out there.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves scary stories about technology and the internet.
